sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: World Model Planners provides tools to prepare recorded robot observations, train world models, evaluate them, and connect a planner to ROS 2.
The repository includes CNN, DINOv2, V-JEPA2, JEPA-lite, and DinoWM model paths, plus a ROS 2 planner bridge.

sections.title: Abstract
paragraphs: Robot learning in simulation has enabled successful transfer to the real world. Yet "real" often means deployment in a controlled environment, whereas "field" deployment exposes a larger reality gap as sites and operating conditions change. We study this distinction in long-horizon navigation using a digital twin of a controlled physical site, simulation-trained predictive representations, and zero-shot physical deployment. Our action-conditioned World Model evaluates candidate trajectories through latent imagination within a shared hierarchical navigation stack. Preliminary trials show lower reference trajectory error for the World Model in the controlled setting, but no corresponding field advantage and substantially lower success rate for path generation than A*.

sections.title: Preliminary Results
paragraphs: In the controlled setting, WM has the lowest ATE but requires more interventions than A* (7 versus 5). That reference-path advantage does not persist in the field. WM also supplies MRP paths half as often as A*. The table shows the quantitative results, and Planner comparison in a difficult building scenario shows the qualitative failure cases.
